major_concerns: Formal verifier may not model vendor-specific semantics (inflated FN/FP).
Mininet/emulation fidelity may miss real-device behaviors limiting external validity.
Prompt sensitivity and LLM stochasticity could dominate measured effects.
required_design_repairs: Preregister precise verifier coverage and limitations; include vendor-mapping or abstraction layer.
Specify emulation scenarios that maximize fidelity and document gaps.
Freeze and publish exact prompts, seeds, and decoding constraints; include prompt-sensitivity ablation.
Define statistical power / sample-size targets and paired-sampling rules.

major_concerns: Repair loops risk overfitting to verifier messages instead of fixing semantics.
Nonconvergence cases and long tails may consume budget and bias results.
Measurement of 'correctness' depends on verifier fidelity and emulation coverage.
required_design_repairs: Preregister iteration bound K, retry policy, and stopping criteria; justify K with pilot data.
Standardize verifier feedback format (machine-readable counterexamples) to reduce prompt-engineering variance.
Include control arms (single-shot and oracle) and seeds; plan analysis for censored/nonconvergent cases.
Budget cap per intent and explicit handling of infrastructure failures in logs.

major_concerns: Ethical risk: publishing adversarial mutations may enable misuse.
Adversarial-generation heuristics may be brittle and nonrepresentative.
Verifier strictness trade-offs may be organization-specific, limiting generality.
required_design_repairs: Add IRB/ethics-style review and explicit non-actionable release policy (redact exploit details).
Preregister adversarial mutation generation procedures with reproducible scripts and constraints to avoid accidental leaks.
Define and freeze verifier rule-sets and justify strict/medium/lenient thresholds; include sensitivity analyses.
Limit published adversarial examples to abstracted summaries and safe-to-release patterns only.

major_concerns: Operator-time estimates may be speculative without field data.
Simulated binary-review decisions oversimplify real operator behavior.
Risk that conclusions depend strongly on assumed review-time distributions.
required_design_repairs: Preregister review-time assumptions and run sensitivity analyses across realistic ranges; cite empirical sources if available.
Model human reviewer behavior probabilistically (allow partial fixes) or justify the binary model.
Include latency and throughput metrics and show Pareto frontier under multiple plausible operator-time models.

major_concerns: Risk of releasing sensitive or realistic vendor commands; dataset representativeness may be limited.
Maintaining benchmark and dataset curation beyond initial release may be resource-constrained.
Synthetic dataset may not capture production heterogeneity.
required_design_repairs: Enforce strict sanitization and synthetic-data provenance; document redaction steps in release.
Provide containerized testbed (Docker) and exact dependency versions to maximize reproducibility.
Preregister dataset composition, inclusion/exclusion rules, and evaluation scripts; include guidance on external validity and limitations.
